Import first. Add location second.

The photo is already on your iPhone. The trip is the missing piece.

Most cameras preserve capture time but record no GPS. LensPin uses that time to place each imported photo against evidence from the same outing.

  1. 1
    Choose the camera photos

    LensPin filters to imported photos without an existing location.

  2. 2
    Add the evidence you have

    Use a timestamped GPX track, nearby geotagged iPhone photos, or both.

  3. 3
    Review every suggestion

    Check the map, time gaps, source agreement, and reason before saving.

Questions before you start

LensPin FAQ

Do I need a GPX file?

No. LensPin can use geotagged iPhone photos taken around the same time. A GPX track usually gives denser evidence, and you can combine both sources.

Does LensPin import photos from my camera?

No. Import with Apple Photos, a compatible card reader, or the camera maker’s workflow first. LensPin begins after the camera photos are in Apple Photos.

What if my camera clock was wrong?

Apply a camera clock offset for matching. It changes the time LensPin compares with the evidence, not the capture time stored on the photo.

What happens when LensPin is not confident?

The photo moves to Review or No Suggestion with an explanation. Conflicting or low-confidence results are not selected as safe defaults.
